english.notes:
(i) Material benefits may include financial benefits, anything which has the potential to result in a financial benefit, and information (section 17C(3)).
(ii) A material benefit is an excluded benefit if it is provided as reasonable consideration for the provision of goods or services, and the provision of those goods or services does not constitute an offence (section 17C(4)).
(iii) A benefit may be provided by or on behalf of a designated body directly or indirectly (for example, it may be provided indirectly through one or more companies) (section 17C(5)).
(iv) The offence may apply to conduct outside the UK but only if the material benefit is or was, or is to be, provided in or from the United Kingdom, or in any case, the person engaging in the conduct is a UK person, or acts for or on behalf of, or holds office under, the Crown, or is in Crown employment (whether or not they engage in the conduct in that capacity).
(v) Where the benefit consists of, or includes, information, and the conduct in question relates to that information, it is a defence to show that the person had a reasonable excuse for that conduct (section 17C(8)).(vi) A person will have a defence when acting under certain obligations or functions (section 17C(9) and (10)).(vii) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
(ix) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023.
